title: Adjoining an n-th root of an element with unit derivative preserves regularity
statement: Let $R$ be a regular ring [def-weil-regular-scheme] (Noetherian, every localization at a prime a regular local ring), let $f\in R$, and let $D:R\to R$ be a derivation (an additive map with $D(ab)=aD(b)+bD(a)$) such that $D(f)$ is a unit of $R$. Then for every integer $n\ge1$ the ring $R[z]/(z^n-f)$, the quotient of the polynomial ring in one variable [def-weil-polynomial-ring] by the ideal generated by $z^n-f$, is a regular ring.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07PG (lemma-degree-p-extension-regular, line 11844), first sentence, and its proof (lines 11851-11857: Algebra Lemma Tag 07NF regular-goes-up gives R[z] regular; Lemma Tag 07PF quotient-regular applied to the extension of D with D(z) = 0)

proof.text: (The extension $\overline D$.) Define $\overline D:R[z]\to R[z]$ coefficientwise [def-weil-polynomial-ring]: $\overline D\bigl(\sum_ir_iz^i\bigr)=\sum_iD(r_i)z^i$. It is additive since $D$ is and addition is coefficientwise. Leibniz rule: for $P=\sum_ip_iz^i$, $Q=\sum_jq_jz^j$ the coefficient of $z^k$ in $PQ$ is $\sum_{i+j=k}p_iq_j$, and $D\bigl(\sum_{i+j=k}p_iq_j\bigr)=\sum_{i+j=k}p_iD(q_j)+\sum_{i+j=k}q_jD(p_i)$, which is the coefficient of $z^k$ in $P\,\overline D(Q)+Q\,\overline D(P)$. So $\overline D$ is a derivation of $R[z]$, and $\overline D(r)=D(r)$ for constants $r\in R$. (In Mathlib this is Derivation.mapCoeffs, Mathlib/RingTheory/Derivation/MapCoeffs.lean:39, and its specialization Differential.mapCoeffs, line 107.)

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07PG, proof, line 11854 ('the extension of $D$ to $R[z]$ which maps $z$ to zero')

proof.text: ($\overline D(z^n-f)$ is a unit modulo $z^n-f$.) $D(1)=D(1\cdot1)=2D(1)$ gives $D(1)=0$, and $D(0)=0$ by additivity; the coefficients of $z^n$ are $0$ and $1$, so $\overline D(z^n)=0$, and $\overline D(z^n-f)=-D(f)$, a constant. As $D(f)$ is a unit of $R$, $-D(f)$ is a unit of $R[z]$ (inverse the constant $-D(f)^{-1}$), hence its image in $R[z]/(z^n-f)R[z]$ is a unit (a ring map sends units to units).

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07PG, proof, lines 11855-11856 ('$D$ annihilates any polynomial with integer coefficients and sends $f$ to a unit')

proof.text: ($R[z]$ is regular.) The ring map $R\to R[z]$ is smooth by [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-smooth] (with $C=R$, $n=1$), and $R$ is a regular ring [def-weil-regular-scheme], so $R[z]$ is a regular ring by the ascent of regularity along smooth maps [lem-weil-pbc-regular-ring-smooth-ascent] (Algebra, Lemma Tag 07NF).

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07PG, proof, lines 11852-11853 (Algebra, Lemma Tag 07NF lemma-regular-goes-up)

proof.text: (Conclusion.) Apply [lem-weil-pbc-hypersurface-derivation-regular] to the regular ring $R[z]$ (Step 3), the element $g=z^n-f\in R[z]$ and the derivation $\overline D$ of $R[z]$ (Step 1), for which the image of $\overline D(g)$ in $R[z]/gR[z]$ is a unit (Step 2). It gives that $R[z]/gR[z]=R[z]/(z^n-f)$ is a regular ring, for every $n\ge1$.
